detailed_analysis: The scientific objective is to resolve distinct sodium environments and flag byproducts in the NLTO product. The data support ONE resolvable 23Na environment: a single narrow, near-symmetric centreband at delta_apparent ~= -4.3 ppm. For 23Na (I=3/2) the isotropic shift is a weak fingerprint (narrow chemical-shift range, offset by field-dependent delta_QIS), so the DISCRIMINATING evidence is the lineshape: a narrow, symmetric line indicates a mobile or high-symmetry (small-EFG, motionally averaged) Na+ site rather than a static, low-symmetry crystallographic site (which would give a broad second-order quadrupolar lineshape). This is consistent with mobile Na+ in an ion conductor. No second-order quadrupolar broadening was resolved and Cq_resolved was not achieved, so no C_Q/eta_Q can be reported as a measurement (only an upper bound). The periodic comb across +/-2000 ppm is a spinning-sideband manifold of this same species with spacing ~87 ppm (nu_r/nu_L), NOT separate byproduct resonances - none of the extra peaks sit off the comb, so no distinct crystalline byproduct (e.g. Na2CO3, NaCl) is cleanly resolved in this single fit. Crucially the fit is only nominally good: the global R^2=0.975 and peak_region_r2=0.980 are inflated by the towering centreband, while the residuals show a coherent comb 10-15x noise (unmodelled higher sidebands) and a large negative trough at the centreband (mismodelled apex/near-wing and unphased negative lobe). The returned negative order_intensities confirm the manifold is compensating rather than fitting the real positive sideband intensity. Because the sidebands are unfit, integrated intensity and centreband fraction (0.94) undercount/mis-partition the true signal, and any quantification of relative Na populations is not defensible from this fit. The MAS rate and nu_L were partly inferred from the comb (metadata sidecar missing), so Hz-based and C_Q-derived values are explicitly provisional.

scientific_claims.claim: The 23Na MAS spectrum of the NLTO product is dominated by a single narrow, near-symmetric centreband at ~-4.3 ppm (apparent) accompanied by a spinning-sideband manifold spaced ~87 ppm (= nu_r/nu_L); no off-comb resonances are resolved, indicating one dominant mobile/high-symmetry (small-EFG) Na+ environment and no cleanly resolved crystalline byproduct in this measurement.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: A single high-symmetry, motionally-averaged Na+ site supports the picture of mobile Na+ carriers in the NLTO ion conductor and argues against significant phase segregation into distinct Na sites/byproducts detectable at this field - directly addressing the objective of resolving Na environments and flagging byproducts.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed a single narrow, near-symmetric 23Na MAS centreband indicating one mobile high-symmetry Na+ environment in sodium-doped lanthanum titanium oxide ion conductors, with sideband intensity confirming a single species rather than multiple crystallographic sites?

Signal: (a) FIRST characterize the periodic comb across ±2000 as spinning sidebands, verifying spacing = ν_r/ν_L using ν_L read from spectrometer_frequency_MHz and ν_r from acquisition metadata; model sidebands as satellites sharing each centreband's shape. (b) The intense narrow feature at ~0 ppm: if it spans multiple points, fit it as a real 23Na centreband (attempt fit_quad_ct; a narrow symmetric line will likely return Cq_resolved=False → pseudo-Voigt FWHM, C_Q as upper bound) — do not mask it. (c) Any residual centrebands NOT lying on the sideband comb: fit with fit_quad_ct (report C_Q/η_Q only when Cq_resolved=True, else pseudo-Voigt FWHM + MQMAS recommendation); use fit_quad_czjzek for washed-out disordered lines. issues.location: Spinning sidebands across the full spectrum (regular comb spaced ~90 ppm, visible at x≈±90, ±100/110, ±185, ±280, ±375, ±468, and out to ±2000)
issues.problem: A single pseudo-Voigt models ONLY the centreband at ~-4.3 ppm. The regular comb of MAS spinning sidebands is completely unmodelled — every sideband is a real, repeating data maximum sitting on a flat/near-zero fit line.

issues.location: Centreband core at x≈-4 to -0.5 ppm
issues.problem: The pseudo-Voigt over/under-shoots the top and near-wings of the tall centreband (derivative-like residual at the apex).

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Fit the sideband manifold: apply fit_sideband_manifold seeded at centre≈-4.3 ppm with mas_rate_ppm≈90–95 ppm (measured from the comb spacing) to capture centreband + sidebands as one species.

verification_iterations.model: Baseline: mask ONLY confirmed single-point DC spikes (verify width at x≈0 first) and edge-fold spikes; low-order polynomial/spline baseline through signal-free windows, with signed amplitudes / re-phasing (NOT a large negative baseline) to handle the negative lobe near 0-100 ppm. Signal: (a) Model the periodic comb across ±2000 ppm as a single MAS spinning-sideband manifold using fit_sideband_manifold, NOT as independent sites. Seed the manifold at centre ≈ -4.3 ppm with mas_rate_ppm ≈ 90–95 ppm measured directly from the comb spacing; cross-check spacing against ν_r/ν_L using ν_L from spectrometer_frequency_MHz and ν_r from acquisition metadata. The manifold captures the centreband at ~-4.3 ppm plus all sideband orders (verified at x≈±90, ±100/110, ±185, ±280, ±375, ±468, out to ±2000) as one species so total integrated intensity and centreband fraction are captured. (b) The intense narrow feature at ~-4.3/0 ppm is the CENTREBAND of this manifold — fit its Voigt width/shape jointly within the manifold; allow the centreband width/shape to refine so the apex and near-wings (currently showing derivative-like residual) are not distorted by unmodelled sideband intensity being absorbed into the wings. If the line remains narrow and symmetric, attempt fit_quad_ct on the centreband (a narrow symmetric line will likely return Cq_resolved=False → report pseudo-Voigt FWHM + C_Q upper bound). (c) Any residual centrebands NOT lying on the sideband comb: fit with fit_quad_ct (report C_Q/η_Q only when Cq_resolved=True, else pseudo-Voigt FWHM + MQMAS recommendation); use fit_quad_czjzek for washed-out disordered lines. Component count set by parsimony (assess_detection on weak features).

issues.problem: The fitted manifold captures the centreband and only the first ~2 sideband orders; the higher-order sidebands are essentially unmodelled. The fit line sits flat/near-zero (or even negative) under real, repeating sideband maxima.

All non-zero sideband orders returned NEGATIVE areas (orders ±1,±2,±3 all negative) while the data sidebands are clearly positive maxima. This is unphysical — the manifold is compensating rather than fitting the real positive sideband intensity.
Derivative-like residual at the tall centreband apex (over/under-shoot of the peak top).

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Re-run fit_sideband_manifold with allow_negative=False and enough orders to span the comb (raise max_order_cap to ~24 and set n_sidebands≈22, ≈2000/87 ppm) so all visible positive sidebands are captured.

quality_history.judge_reasoning: Both attempts are fundamentally the same in outcome: they fit only the intense centreband at ~-4 ppm with a single pseudo-Voigt and leave the entire spinning-sideband manifold unmodelled. In both residual panels, a regular comb of positive spikes extends across the full ±2000 ppm range, each spike corresponding to a real, repeating spinning sideband that the model does not capture. This is a clear, coherent systematic pattern (not noise), with residual peaks reaching ~10-15x the noise level and a large negative residual trough around the centreband indicating the peak shape/baseline is also mismodelled (derivative-like/undershoot near the apex). The high R² (~0.975) is misleading because it is dominated by the enormously intense centreband; the sidebands carry small absolute amplitude but are unambiguously real, physically meaningful features (MAS spinning sidebands) that any acceptable NMR fit of this data must model. Neither attempt actually implemented the sideband manifold — Attempt 1 describes an elaborate sideband strategy in its model text but the visualization shows the identical unmodelled comb as Attempt 2. Since the dominant real feature (the sideband manifold and the negative lobe near the centreband) is left unfit in both, neither is physically acceptable.
